learning_outcomes.text: Can able to solve problems related to engine cycles.
Be able to understand the main engine components and functions and the working principle of the internal combustion engines.
Can apply thermodynamics of gas mixtures.
Can apply engine mechanics and engine balancing.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION: Engine classification, classification and operation principles of internal combustion engines.
IDEAL CYCLES: Otto and Diesel cycle analysis, I. Experiment.
IDEAL CYCLES: Combined cycle analysis and comparison of Otto, Diesel and Hybrid cycles .
COMBUSTION AND MIXTURE ENERGY: Fuels and their chemical properties. Combustion chemistry. Thermal value of mixtures.
AIR FUEL CYCLES: Analysis of air-fuel cycles by using graphics.
REAL CYCLES: Real cycles properties. Combustion rate. Processes occurring in the cycle. Specific fuel consumption.
REAL CYCLES: Air capacity and volumetric efficiency. Flame speed and factors influencing the speed of the flame speed.
REAL CYCLES: Engine knocking. Ignition delay and affecting factors.
FUEL-AIR induction: Carburetors and the desired properties. Venturi and fuel nozzle calculations. Carburetor additional fittings.
FUEL-AIR induction: The advantages and disadvantages of injection systems. Classification of injection systems.
ENGINE MECHANICS: Analysis of the movement of the piston. Forces acting on engine elements. Flywheel mass calculation.
ENGINE BALANCE: Single-cylinder engine balancing. Balancing multi-cylinder engines.
ENGINE BALANCE: Single-cylinder engine balancing. Balancing multi-cylinder engines.
bibliography: H. Sezgin, Internal Combustion Engine Design, 1975.
Engineering Fundamentals of the Internal Combustion Engine, W. W. Pulkrabek, Prentice Hall,1997.
Internal Combustion Engine Fundamentals, J. P.
